provider_policy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which system holds the authoritative identifier for this test case, and what identifier value does it issue?
Which alternate or legacy identifiers must resolve to this test case, and in which external systems do they live?
What identity guarantees hold when the test case is renamed, moved between repositories or migrated between tools?
What distinguishes one test case from a variant, a duplicate and a differently-named copy of the same test?
How is a new revision of the test case definition created, numbered and superseded?
Who authored or changed this revision, on what authority, and from which prior revision was it derived?
Which timestamps distinguish when a revision became effective from when the register recorded it?
Which changes to a definition require a new revision rather than an in-place editorial correction?
How can a consumer prove that the definition referenced by a past execution has not been altered?
What single objective does this test case exist to verify, stated independently of how it is executed?
Which test level, test type and quality characteristic classify this test case, and from which controlled vocabulary?
Which test item, component or interface is under test, and how is it referenced?
How is the objective checked for being single-purpose, observable and falsifiable?
Which requirement, acceptance-criterion, risk or specification statements does this test case revision trace to, and with what link type?
Which coverage items does this test case cover, and which test design technique produced them?
Which normative statement gives the expected outcome its authority, and what is its prescription level?
How is traceability completeness assessed without asserting one-to-one coverage of a requirement?
Was the case written manually, derived from a model, or generated combinatorially, and with which generation parameters?
What state must the test item, its data and the referenced environment be in before execution begins?
Which preconditions are mandatory gates and which are advisory assumptions that merely make the case inapplicable?
How is each precondition established: by the case itself, by a referenced fixture, or by an external set-up step?
What disposition does the definition declare when a precondition cannot be established?
Which fixtures and test data sets does this case require, and how are they referenced and versioned?
What sensitivity classification applies to the referenced test data, and is production-derived data permitted for this case?
Which parts of the referenced data are inputs, which are seeded state and which are expected baselines?
What determinism and isolation guarantees must the data satisfy for the expected outcome to hold?
How long must a referenced data set remain resolvable for past evidence to stay interpretable?
Which parameters does the test case declare, with what types, defaults and value constraints?
When a parameter set produces many invocations, what is the identity of each variant relative to the parent test case?
On what sampling, boundary or interaction basis are the input values or ranges chosen?
Which parameter combinations are excluded as invalid, unreachable or unsafe?
How are parameter values bound at resolution time from external configuration or credential stores?
What is the ordered sequence of actions the test case prescribes, and at what granularity is a step defined?
How is an individual step identified so that expected outcomes and captured evidence can attach to it?
Which steps are shared set-up or teardown and which are the discriminating actions of this case?
Is the step order significant, and which steps may be reordered, repeated or run concurrently?
Where a step delegates to a reusable keyword or shared step definition, how is that reference resolved?
What outcome must a conforming test item produce, stated per step and for the case overall?
Which comparison rule, tolerance and units apply when the expected outcome is numeric or approximate?
Which reference baseline or golden artifact does the comparison use, and how is it versioned?
Which parts of an observed outcome are normalized, masked or ignored before comparison?
What agreement criterion does the definition fix, and what is explicitly left for result adjudication to decide?
What state must hold after the case completes, independently of the outcome it produced?
Which cleanup or restoration obligations does the case declare, and who performs them?
Which downstream cases depend on state that this case deliberately leaves behind?
Which side effects are permitted, and which must never escape the test boundary?
Which executable implementation realises this test case revision, and how is it addressed?
Which automation framework contract must the implementation satisfy for the binding to be valid?
How is a binding detected as broken, ambiguous or pointing at a different revision than intended?
Is this case manual, automatable, automated or generated, and who decides that status?
What must remain true of the definition when only the implementation changes?
Which tags, attributes and priority values are declared for selection, and from which vocabulary?
Under which product configurations, platforms, locales or feature flags is this case applicable?
Which other test cases must have succeeded, or must not run concurrently, for this case to be meaningful?
What selection expression would an agent evaluate to include this case in a given scope, and which model owns evaluating and scheduling it?
Is applicability time-bounded, for example pending a fix, a deprecation date or a seasonal window?
Which role or team owns this test case definition, and who maintains it day to day?
Which readiness states can a definition revision hold, and which transitions between them are permitted?
Who may approve a revision as ready for execution, and on what basis?
Who may read, propose changes to and publish this definition, and which parts are restricted?
Which review criteria must a revision satisfy before it is marked ready?
Which system of record issues the authoritative identifier for this execution record, and what is that identifier?
When no master-system identifier exists, which governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID stands in, and how is that substitution marked?
Which stable correlation key groups executions that are logically the same check across different runs?
What constraint prevents a date, a status value, a display name or a test-case identifier from acting as the record key?
Which immutable test-case revision, and which version of its expected-result or oracle definition, does this execution bind to?
Which criterion or rule was evaluated, in which rule version and by which tool component version?
What concrete parameter values, data-set references and randomisation seeds were bound for this execution?
What happens to this record if the referenced test case is subsequently modified, deprecated or withdrawn?
Which run, suite or campaign contains this execution, and what identifies that container authoritatively?
Which build, artifact or source revision was under test, identified by digest rather than by label?
Which environment or configuration item hosted the execution, and which model owns that record?
Which actor, harness or tool executed the case, in which version, and under what observed invocation?
What minimum context set must be present before this record may be treated as reproducible?
What are the start and end times of this attempt, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
When was each outcome observed by the executing agent, and when was the record ingested, and do these differ from the event time?
What duration is reported, measured from which clock and at what resolution?
How are unsynchronised, unknown-offset or reconstructed timestamps represented without fabricating precision?
What is this attempt's ordinal within the retry group, and which earlier attempt does it directly follow?
What triggered this retry — harness policy, orchestration rule or human decision — and which policy record applies?
Which rule guarantees that an earlier attempt's observations, timestamps and attachments cannot be mutated by a later attempt?
When attempts in one group disagree, how is the group-level outcome reported and which attempt is authoritative?
What actual value, output or system state was observed, and in what representation was it captured?
Against which expected value or oracle was the observation compared, and by which comparator?
What tolerance, precision, normalisation or masking was applied before the comparison was judged?
Where in the subject does this observation apply, expressed as a pointer, location or region?
How is an observation that could not be evaluated recorded without asserting either pass or fail?
Which ordered steps or assertions were executed, and what outcome does each carry in its own right?
At which step did execution first deviate, and were the following steps executed, skipped or blocked?
How is the container or suite outcome derived from member outcomes, and is that derivation itself recorded?
What distinguishes a step from a nested sub-test, and how deep may the hierarchy legitimately go?
Which governed verdict value applies to this execution, and what is that value's precise definition in the adopting Dimension?
Who or what asserted the verdict, in which mode, and on whose authority?
Which recorded observations and which oracle support this verdict, and was it derived or directly reported?
Which verdict and evidence combinations are prohibited, such as a pass with no evaluated expectation or a pass inferred from an absent defect?
How does this verdict map onto external vocabularies, and which mappings lose information?
Across which attempt set, under which proven-identical binding, did the observed outcomes disagree?
How is this execution classified — deterministic, flaky, environment-induced or unknown — and on what evidence?
May a non-determinism classification change the reported verdict, and which role is permitted to decide that?
What instability measure is reported, over which observation window and with which denominator?
Which states may an execution record occupy, and which transitions between them are legal?
Which revision supersedes which, for what reason, by whom, and effective from when?
What distinguishes a correction of an adjudication from a new execution attempt, and which must be used in each case?
For how long must a superseded revision remain retrievable, and which policy owns that decision?
Which evidence artifacts were captured for this attempt, and what role does each one play?
To which attempt, step or observation is each attachment bound, and may one attachment serve several of them?
Do captures contain personal data, secrets or customer content, and what redaction was applied before storage?
Where is each artifact stored, and which reference stays meaningful if the store is rotated or purged?
Which digest algorithm and value seals each evidence artifact and each emitted result document?
Which signed attestation, if any, binds this result to the subject under test, and under which predicate type?
What integrity-check outcome has a verifying system reported back, and how is it recorded here without this model performing the check?
What minimum integrity metadata must be present before this result may be exported as release evidence?
Which defect or issue records does this execution reference, and in which role — raised, reproduced, verified-fixed or known-issue?
Which model or system owns each referenced record's lifecycle, and which of its fields must never be copied into this record?
What rule prevents a pass verdict from being inferred from the absence of a linked defect or an empty failure list?
Which build or release records consume this evidence, and is that reference maintained here, at the consumer, or in both places?
Which interchange format and schema version was emitted, and which semantics does that projection lose?
How do record identifiers survive projection into formats that identify tests only by name, class or ordinal?
Which representation is authoritative when the emitted projection and the internal record disagree?
How is an emitted document checked against its declared schema, and what is recorded when it does not validate?
Which accountable party owns this test case or test result record and the assurance claims derived from it?
Which steward maintains the record day to day, and under what delegated authority do they act?
Which custodian holds the stored evidence when custody is separated from record ownership?
What evidence records a transfer of ownership, and from which moment did it take effect?
Which roles must have acted before a test case revision may reach an approved state?
Which role combinations are prohibited on the same record revision?
How is the executor's independence from the author demonstrated at the applicable integrity level?
Which documented exception permits a role conflict on this record, and who granted it?
Which lifecycle states are defined for a test case definition, and which for a test result record?
Which transitions require review and approval before the record becomes usable as evidence?
What signature manifestation is captured when a record is approved?
How is an approval bound to the exact revision it approved rather than to the record as a whole?
Under what conditions may an approved record be returned to an earlier state, and what is recorded?
How is a revision of a test case identified, and what change makes it a new test case instead?
Under what rule is an approved or finalised record corrected, by edit or by superseding revision?
Which timestamps establish the validity window of a revision that has been superseded?
What happens to test results that reference a test case revision after that revision is superseded?
Which agent, acting under which plan and activity, produced this test result?
How are execution event time, observation time and ingestion time recorded separately for one run?
How is the tool, harness or generator that produced the result identified and trust-assessed?
Which environment and resolved dependency facts form part of the execution record?
What does this provenance record explicitly not attest about the run?
What digest and algorithm bind an evidence artifact to the result record that cites it?
How is an evidence artifact shown to be unaltered after ingestion?
At what point does evidence become immutable, and what may still change afterwards?
How is a failed or unverifiable integrity check represented rather than discarded?
Which mandatory fields and referential links must resolve before a result record is accepted?
How is an inconclusive, blocked, aborted or errored execution outcome represented?
What confidence grade is attached to a result, and on what basis is it assigned?
How is a known-unreliable or intermittently failing test flagged without deleting its records?
What limit does this model state on what a passing result establishes?
Which coverage item type, measurement method and denominator does this figure refer to?
Which scope boundaries and exclusions limit this coverage figure?
Which executions and definition revisions were aggregated to produce the figure?
What caveat is carried so the figure is not read as proof of adequacy?
How is a coverage claim referenced by an external gate without this model owning that gate?
Which requirement, risk or control does this test case assert that it exercises?
Who asserted this trace link, and when was it last reconfirmed?
What happens to the trace link when the referenced target revision changes?
How is a trace link expressed so an external tool can resolve it without local knowledge?
What sensitivity label applies to this record, and does it differ for individual fields or artifacts?
Do the test inputs, logs or attachments contain personal or production-derived data?
Which minimisation or pseudonymisation measure was applied before the data entered the record?
Which fields must be masked for a reader holding only baseline access?
Which retention rule and disposition authority governs this record class?
When does the retention clock start for the result, and when for its evidence artifacts?
Which legal hold suspends disposition, and who may place or release it?
What remains after disposition: full erasure, redacted stub or tombstone?
Which redaction profile applies when a test record leaves its home boundary?
How is integrity re-established for an export whose content has been redacted?
What does the export manifest tell the recipient about what was withheld?
Which approval is required before an export crosses an organisational or jurisdictional boundary?
Which external standard, schema or vocabulary does a given field set claim to align with?
What evidence would be required before a conformance claim to that standard could be made?
Where do two aligned standards conflict, and how is that conflict held open?
Which regional or sector-specific rule changes the governance obligations for these records?
How is a tool-specific report format bound without becoming this model's semantics?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
